In #43777, I implement a linter for redundant uses of <|, such as: Nat.succ <| 0, Nat.succ <| (0), List.cons 0 <| [1] or [0,1].foldl (init := 0) <| fun a b ↦ a + b.

I think this will help make mathlib's style more uniform. I'm not familiar with the promised autoformatter, but my guess is that it will not suggest changing the syntax, only changing how it is formatted, so this should be orthogonal.

What do you think of the idea? If this goes well, we could also add more such linters, such as for |>. notation.

I often find myself using the technically redundant <| in your last example for (my own) readability, for whatever reason it otherwise takes me a moment to parse that fun ... has the required precedence. (Ofc that shouldn't decide anything, i'm used to reading eg Mathlib code without the extra <|.)
I've had a case where I wrote Subtype.ext <| foo _ for a bunch of fields of a structure, even though in some cases there were no underscores.
@Eric Wieser, did you also align the := of the structure fields? I'm pretty sure that any autoformatter will complain about that as well.
No, I didn't go that far, and I do see the analogy

I have now modified the linter so that it does not complain about some cases where <| notation might make things easier to read: in particular <| fun ..., <| ! ... and <| ¬ ... are now not linted against.

To my surprise, the linter still gives almost 1000 warnings. I have split the adaptations out in #44067, which was generated with the help of ./scripts/runSkimmer.sh
